title: Local Adaptive Inference with LISA
text: Start 3D volume small planted blob. Build null spec permuted maps, build filter, call lisa() — q-value map rejection mask come back single neurothresh_result. Mid-axial slice planted-blob example: input Z, filtered statistic, q-value map, LISA rejection mask. blob lights filtered map (smoother peak), survives q ≤ 0.10, rejection mask localises without bleeding far outside true support.
code: ns <- null_from_maps(z, nulls) filt <- lisa_bilateral(radius = 1, n_iter = 1) fit <- lisa(stat_vol = ns$stat_vol, mask = ns$mask, null_spec = ns,             filter = filt,             tail = "pos", q = 0.10) fit #> <neurothresh_result> #>   method   : lisa  #>   q        : 0.1  #>   tail     : pos  #>   threshold: 4.604  #>   rejected : 72 / 1000 voxels (7.20%)

title: Local Adaptive Inference with LISA
text: LISA four objects compose: pipeline always shape: build inputs → build null spec → build filter → call lisa() → inspect result. wrappers lisa_onesample(), lisa_twosample(), lisa_glm() chain steps 1–3 common designs.

title: Local Adaptive Inference with LISA
text: filter two scales: sigma_space controls far physical neighbourhood filter averages — bigger σ pools across voxels. sigma_range controls much statistic disagreement tolerated — bigger σ pools across value differences (less edge-preserving). radius caps neighbourhood ±r voxels. n_iter > 1 re-applies filter, sharpening edges. LISA uses neuroim2::bilateral_filter(), whose neighborhoods mask-normalized default, edge voxels dragged toward --mask --bounds zeros.  tight filter behaves close voxelwise inference: preserves edges pools little. loose filter behaves like cluster inference: blob spreads soft halo. default sits . usually want defaults; reach tighter settings peaks dense edges matter, looser settings effects diffuse.
code: filters <- list(   tight   = lisa_bilateral(radius = 1, sigma_space = 0.7, sigma_range = 1,                             n_iter = 1),   default = lisa_bilateral(radius = 1, n_iter = 1),   loose   = lisa_bilateral(radius = 1, sigma_space = 1.5, sigma_range = 4,                             n_iter = 1) ) filtered <- lapply(filters, function(f) {   fit_f <- lisa(stat_vol = ns$stat_vol, mask = ns$mask, null_spec = ns,                 filter = f, tail = "pos", q = 0.10)   as.numeric(lisa_filtered_stat(fit_f)) })

title: Local Adaptive Inference with LISA
text: subject-level images, lisa_onesample() wrapper builds null spec using null_one_sample(). tail, q, filter, storage arguments flow . Two-group designs use lisa_twosample(imgs, group, ...). Anything involved — covariates, nuisance regressors, -subject contrasts — uses lisa_glm(imgs, design, contrast, ...) recommended path whenever analysis strictly one- two-sample.
code: imgs <- replicate(8, plant_blob(make_smooth(), amp = 2.5), simplify = FALSE) one <- lisa_onesample(   imgs,   n_perm = 24,   seed = 1,   filter = lisa_bilateral(radius = 1, n_iter = 1),   tail = "pos",   q = 0.20 ) one #> <neurothresh_result> #>   method   : lisa  #>   q        : 0.2  #>   tail     : pos  #>   threshold: 1.166  #>   rejected : 91 / 1000 voxels (9.10%)

code: library(neurothresh)

title: Simulation Validation: FWER and Power
text: First, let’s check ’s signal (pure noise), reject 5% time using α = 0.05. ’ll use simple 2D example soft-max score. estimated FWER neighborhood 0.05. variation expected vignette uses 200 fresh null samples. null distribution defines decision threshold. Fresh null simulations crossing red line become false positives.
code: # Simulation parameters B <- 200       # Number of null simulations to build threshold n <- 30        # Grid size (30 x 30) kernel <- make_kernel(radius = 2, sigma = 1)  # Step 1: Build null distribution by simulating pure noise null_scores <- numeric(B) for (b in seq_len(B)) {   z <- matrix(rnorm(n * n), nrow = n)   z <- smooth_field(z, kernel)  # Add spatial correlation   null_scores[b] <- softmax_score(z, kappa = 1) }  # Step 2: Set threshold at 95th percentile (for alpha = 0.05) threshold <- quantile(null_scores, probs = 0.95)  # Step 3: Check false positive rate with fresh null samples B2 <- 200 false_positives <- 0 for (b in seq_len(B2)) {   z <- matrix(rnorm(n * n), nrow = n)   z <- smooth_field(z, kernel)   false_positives <- false_positives + (softmax_score(z, kappa = 1) >= threshold) }  fwer_estimate <- false_positives / B2 cat("Estimated FWER:", fwer_estimate, "\n") #> Estimated FWER: 0.045 cat("Expected (alpha = 0.05):", 0.05, "\n") #> Expected (alpha = 0.05): 0.05
